exposure: physician status (female physician or spouse of male physician)
driving factors for CD (lack of confidence in intrapartum fetal monitoring, uncertainty of vaginal delivery outcome, fear of labor pain, obstetricians' fear of blame)
outcome: rate of CD for maternal request (CDMR)
rate of repeat elective CD among TOLAC candidates
cohort: The participants were parous female physicians (n=15) and parous spouses of male physicians (n=86) practicing at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital.
finding: The study revealed a significantly higher overall cesarean delivery rate (44.3%) among physicians and their spouses compared to the general Ethiopian population, driven by factors such as lack of confidence in monitoring, fear of labor pain, and fear of blame.
mod_finding: The study found an 81 (44.3%) overall cesarean delivery rate among the physician community, with 95% of potential Trial of Labor after Cesarean delivery (TOLAC) candidates opting for repeat elective CD.
